pr_title: Fix mask behaviour when service is enabled
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
<!--- Describe the change below, including rationale and design decisions -->
Mask and enabled operations are actually mutually exclusive ones.
So if service is enabled, it can't be masked at the same time.
As a result we need to mask service after it being disabled and unmask
it before enabling.

Currently mask just do not work if service is enabled, so module needs
to be runned twice to apply
{enabled: false, masked: true} on enabld service.
This behaviour should be fixed now.
Fixes: #68680 
<!--- HINT: Include "Fixes #nnn" if you are fixing an existing issue -->

##### ISSUE TYPE
<!--- Pick one below and delete the rest -->
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
<!--- Write the short name of the module, plugin, task or feature below -->
systemd
pr_comments: @bcoca It would be great to receive a review....

I'm against doing it mutually exclusive. Then if you need to start service and make it enabled you will need 2 systemd tasks in a row. Eventually you may never know when service is masked or not, so you will need 2 tasks for that anytime you want to start service after reboot (which is very wide use case) which is kind of code duplication in playbooks.

> I'm against doing it mutually exclusive. Then if you need to start service and make it enabled you will need 2 systemd tasks in a row. 

Good point. I'll re-review it with this behavior in mind.

I've been putting together a test matrix and I think these are the combinations in which the module would fail with an error stating the unit is masked. I think most of these make sense and can be fixed setting the correct parameters for the module in a single task.

|Service Masked     | Service Enabled   | Service State |   | Masked (Param) | Enabled (Param) | State (Param)
|-------------------|-------------------|---------------|---|---|---|---|
| any | any | any | | True | True | - |
| True | False | any | | - | True | - |
| any | any | stopped | | True | - | started
| any | any | any | | True | - | restarted
| any | any | any | | True | - | reloaded

I put together a [rough set of tasks](https://gist.github.com/samdoran/fd1b56ce8bee34c50cb890f0325e56ec) that can be used for the integration tests. It's a pretty rough list, but should serve as a general model. The trickiest part is needing to test the combination of module parameters with the combination of system states to make sure the module does the right thing in all circumstances.
Thanks so much, I will take some tome during this week to look into it more carefully

I think this has been partially fixed now with newer systemd version. So for example, now it's allowed to mask enabled service - systemd will automatically disable service when it get mask request.

review_comments: If we make `enabled` and `masked` mutually exclusive, this section of code is unnecessary.

```suggestion
                # Run masked_action when enabled param is not provided or service is supposed to be enabled/started.
                if not module.check_mode and module.params['enabled'] in [None, True]):
```

I feel like the masking behavior should be to unmask the service if it is to be started or enabled. Since `systmed` cannot start or enable a masked service, the conditional in line 437 can be removed and the masking/unmasking should always happen.

I'm also not really sure about that. I think if service is masked, it might be a reason for it, and we shouldn't just enable masked service until it's explicitly told, so user should be aware what exactly he is doing. And it's kind of current behaviour (except it's not fully working). As generally services doesn't appear masked - they are explicitly told to take that state.
